title: Headroom stitching playbook (capacity pulse to optimize)
summary: Working spreadsheet and playbook that stitches short-term product telemetry (pulse metrics) into weekly GPU capacity guidance for Redwood Optimize. Focus is on producing a small number of actionable knobs (reserve GPUs, burst headroom, batch target) and feeding the outputs into the cost optimizer and billing attribution sheets.
purpose: Create a reproducible pipeline from product metrics -> forecast scenarios -> GPU headroom recommendation. Make the steps traceable and human-reviewable so on-call, product, and infra can agree on reserve commits and burst sizing each week.
key_assumptions: 1) Token-per-request distribution is stable within +/-20% for a given feature. 2) Batching efficiency is correlated with concurrent request count; empirical multiplier derived from serving-runtime traces. 3) Effective throughput per GPU is measured as tokens/sec under p95 latency SLO. 4) Customers can tolerate a planned 5%-15% request-shed fallback during extreme microbursts.
sheet_descriptions: raw-traffic-pulse: raw daily/5m QPS and request types from telemetry. token-distribution-sampler: bootstrap sampler to simulate per-request token counts by feature. gpu-profiles-and-benchmarks: normalized tokens/sec per GPU by model variant + quantization profile. headroom-stitch: core logic that converts forecasted tokens/sec to number of GPUs needed, includes safety buffer and burst margin. cost-traceback: maps GPUs to unit cost and per-request cost. scenario-simulations: deterministic scenarios (linear growth, step jumps, localized bursts). weekly-action-log: decisions, owners, linked PRs/commits.
calc_formulas: effective_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = benchmark_tokens_sec * quantization_efficiency * kernel_utilization_factor; required_gpus = ceil( forecasted_tokens_per_sec / (effective_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * operational_utilization_target) ); headroom_gpu = round(required_gpus * (1 + planned_burst_margin_pct)); reserved_commit = max(min_commit, floor(required_gpus * reserve_pct));
example_walkthrough: Example: product pulse shows 250k tokens/sec baseline for chat-feature-A at 9:00 PST. Benchmark for model-x on a4:tp shows 125k tokens/sec baseline. Quantization/merge efficiency for this workload = 0.78; kernel_utilization_factor = 0.9; operational_utilization_target = 0.72. effective_tokens = 125k * 0.78 * 0.9 = ~87.75k. required_gpus = ceil(250k / (87.75k * 0.72)) = ceil(250k / 63.18k) = 4. headroom_gpu with planned_burst_margin_pct 25% -> 5 GPUs. Reserved_commit floor 3 -> reserve 3, plan burst capacity to 5 via burst policy.
sensitivity_tests: batching-degradation: efficiency drops to 60% at low concurrency
recommended_knobs: reserve_pct: fraction of required_gpus to commit as reserved (default 60%)
batch_target_tokens: recommended batching policy per model/route
actions_and_recommendations: 1) Weekly cadence: run 'raw-traffic-pulse' -> regenerate forecast for next 14 days, update headroom-stitch, and check scenario-simulations for any collapse points. 2) For upcoming week, if required_gpus delta > 1.0 relative to current reserved commit, escalate to infra and sales-ops for commit decision. 3) When simulated cost-per-req increases > 12% under 2x burst test, run a quick quantization recommendation experiment (redwood-optimize bench run) before committing extra reserved capacity. 4) Add a canary route with reduced batch_target to measure real batching_decay under low concurrency before changing reserve policy.
operational_playbook: - Monday 09:00 PST: owner runs the sheet, records recommended reserve and burst numbers in weekly-action-log. - Update cost-traceback and notify finance slack channel with delta. - If headroom recommendation requires >10% additional reserved spend, schedule 1:1 with demand owner. - On-call SRE: verify autoscaler policy matches planned_burst_margin_pct; confirm fallback policies and model-variant routing are in place.
open_questions: 1) Do we have high-quality per-route token histograms for all enterprise customers? (some customers still aggregate at app-level). 2) Should we bake customer-pricing elasticity into reserve decision or keep it separate? 3) How to encode multi-region fanout costs in cost-traceback without double counting egress?
next_steps: Instrument a daily job to export 5m product pulses to the raw-traffic-pulse tab (owner: Jamal)
Run a 2-week backtest comparing headroom-stitch outputs against actual scaling events (owner: Priya)
Prototype a simple alert if required_gpus increases > 30% in 24h (owner: Liam)
notes_for_reviewers: This is a working draft: core logic in headroom-stitch is intentionally conservative. Please flag if your team has empirical throughput numbers different from gpu-profiles-and-benchmarks. Prefer short feedback in the weekly-action-log rather than long threads.
content:
Raw narrative & scratch notes below:

- Motivation: Operations and product have different mental models for "how much GPU". This sheet tries to be the single source that both sides can point to: inputs are product-level pulse metrics; outputs are reserve + burst guidance and a simple cost delta.

- Why 'stitching': we combine heterogeneous signals (telemetry QPS, per-request token distributions, serving runtime benchmarks, and business SLA constraints) — the stitch is the deterministic math + safety heuristics that make these signals actionable.

- Quick glossary: pulse = high-freq telemetry exports; headroom = extra GPUs beyond steady-state reserve to accommodate bursts; reserve = committed monthly capacity; burst = short-term elastic capacity that can exceed reserve.

- Quick heuristics used historically: target utilization 70-75% to avoid tail latency blow-ups; reserve floor equals last-month average required_gpus rounded down to nearest integer unless clear growth detected.

- Things to avoid: relying on 1-day spikes to set reserve; double counting token compression improvements when forecasting both model rollouts and quantization improvements in same window.

End of sheet draft.
format_notes: This file is a sheet representation (text-first) to document calculation logic and owner workflow. The canonical numeric workbook lives in the same folder as an actual Google Sheet; this doc explains tabs, formulas, and decision policy.
privacy_and_security: Contains aggregated product telemetry only; no PII or customer raw transcripts. Spreadsheet-level access should remain limited to product, infra, and finance during planning windows.
